gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Amazfit's iPhone reply feature (iOS Notification Forwarding, in beta) works only in the European Union, needs iOS 26.5 or later and launched on just the Cheetah 2 Ultra, Balance Ultra and Balance 3. So a US iPhone owner cannot reply to messages from the Active Max, Bip 6 or Bip Max. The Bip Max is only on the list of models to get it later.
standout_why: I compared against our own page and ChatGPT's three answers. Our page and the answers only say replies are Android-only or that you 'generally cannot reply to iMessages'. None of them mentions that Amazfit has shipped iPhone replies at all, or that they are limited to the EU, to iOS 26.5 or later, and to certain models. A shopper who has read the 2026 news about iPhone replies would read our page as out of date. I could not open the cited us.amazfit.com Bip 6 page (HTTP 429 on every try) or the Tom's Guide body (the fetch returned only the title), so I can't rule out a footnote on those pages. Their visible snippets and ChatGPT's answers show no such footnote. A smaller gap: the cited Bip 6 listing and Amazfit's support docs still say iOS 14.0, but the current Zepp app in the US App Store requires iOS 15.0.
decides: It confirms the pick but doesn't change it. For a US iPhone buyer under $200, the Active Max, Bip 6 and Bip Max all get notifications and calls but no replies. The EU-only reply beta doesn't cover the Active Max or Bip 6, and for the Bip Max it is only promised. So replies shouldn't separate them, and the choice still comes down to battery and price. A shopper who needs replies has to leave Amazfit's under-$200 line for the Apple Watch SE 3, which fails the two-week battery requirement.
